title: What If a Tree Stood Alone for 250 Miles? A Truck Still Hit It

scenes.text: What if a tree were the only one for 250 miles? Somebody still drove into it.
The Tree of Ténéré was an acacia in the Sahara, in Niger. No other tree for 400 kilometers in any direction.
It stood about 300 years. Salt caravans steered by it, and it was marked on maps of the desert.
In the 1930s, a well dug beside it showed how it survived: its roots reached water about 35 meters down.
Then in 1973, a truck driver, reportedly drunk, knocked it down. In all that empty desert.
The dead trunk now stands in Niger's national museum. Where it grew, there is a tree made of metal.

description:
What if a tree were the only one for 250 miles in every direction? The Tree of Ténéré, a lone acacia in the Sahara in Niger, was once considered the most isolated tree on Earth.
It was a landmark on the caravan routes for about 300 years. When a well was dug beside it in the winter of 1938 to 1939, its roots were found reaching the water table 33 to 36 meters down. In 1973 it was knocked over by a truck driver who was reportedly drunk. The trunk was moved to the Niger National Museum in Niamey that November, and a simple metal sculpture marks the spot. Guinness now lists a spruce on Campbell Island, 222 km from its nearest neighbour, as the remotest tree.
